sop_modules.name: Setup — Glass Masking, Hardware Removal, Adjacent Surface Protection, Landscape/Hardscape Protection, Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Full setup module for exterior window repaint. Glass masking is MANDATORY regardless of method — largest single protection task (30-40% of total time for TDL windows). Three masking methods: tape-and-film (standard), liquid mask (TDL non-Low-E only), TDL individual pane tape (TDL + Low-E). Hardware removal preferred (labeled bags per window). Weatherstrip protection (remove or deep-tape — NEVER paint weatherstripping). Sill/casing/siding adjacent surface protection (RP: all adjacent surfaces are almost always already finished). Landscape/hardscape ground protection (RP-specific — catches scraping debris, power wash runoff, paint drips). Equipment setup (brush or spray). Mostly DIRECT transfers from NC MOD_XWIN_SETUP with 2 RP-specific landscape/hardscape tasks added.

tasks.name: Glass Masking — Tape and Static-Cling Film
tasks.description: Apply HDPE static-cling film and tape to window glass panes. Standard method for single-lite, SDL, and GBG windows. Film covers glass area, tape seals at frame edge. 1/16-inch glass lap line must remain exposed for weather seal. MANDATORY regardless of application method.
tasks.notes: Standard masking method. GBG grilles between glass — mask as single lite. SDL simulated divided lite — mask as single lite (applied bars are on exterior of sealed IG unit).

tasks.name: Glass Masking — Liquid Mask (TDL Non-Low-E)
tasks.description: Apply liquid masking product (Masking Liquid H2O) to individual TDL glass panes. Brush on, allow to dry, peel after painting. Significant labor savings on multi-pane TDL windows vs individual pane taping. PROHIBITED on Low-E glass — scoring to remove damages Low-E coating permanently.
tasks.notes: HARD STOP: Low-E glass = false required. Low-E coating is permanently damaged by liquid mask scoring.

tasks.name: Glass Masking — Individual Pane Tape (TDL + Low-E)
tasks.description: Apply tape and film to each individual TDL glass pane. Required when TDL windows have Low-E glass (liquid mask prohibited). Highest masking labor — each small pane masked individually with precision tape at muntin bars. Major cost driver for TDL Low-E windows.
tasks.notes: Most expensive masking path. TDL + Low-E forces individual pane taping.

tasks.name: Remove Window Hardware
tasks.description: Remove all operable window hardware (locks, lifts, sash pulls, crank handles). Bag and label per window. RP consideration: existing hardware may have paint buildup requiring careful scoring before removal. Fixed windows have no operable hardware — skip.
tasks.notes: Skip for fixed windows (no operable hardware). RP: score paint buildup at hardware edges before removal to prevent paint tear-out.

tasks.name: Protect Weatherstripping
tasks.description: Remove friction-fit weatherstripping or deep-tape non-removable weatherstripping on operable sashes. NEVER paint weatherstripping — destroys elasticity and seal function. Fixed windows: skip.
tasks.notes: NEVER paint weatherstripping. Fixed windows have no weatherstripping — skip.

tasks.name: Protect Exterior Sill
tasks.description: Tape and paper/film over finished exterior sill to prevent drips and overspray. In RP, sill is almost always already finished — protection is mandatory for both brush and spray.
tasks.notes: RP: sill almost always already finished. Protection mandatory for both brush and spray methods.

tasks.name: Protect Adjacent Window Casing
tasks.description: Light tape at casing-to-frame junction when casing is already finished. Minimal masking — tape only at junction line. In RP, casing is almost always already finished.
tasks.notes: RP: casing almost always already finished. Window casing painting belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_RP — this spec protects the junction.

tasks.name: Mask Adjacent Siding (Spray Only)
tasks.description: Paper and tape protection on finished siding around window perimeter. Required for spray application only — prevents overspray on siding field. 12-24 inches from window edge. Not needed for brush work.
tasks.notes: Spray only. If siding RP is also in scope on same elevation, coordinate masking ownership.

tasks.name: Equipment Setup — Brush
tasks.description: Set up brush painting equipment: organize brushes (1.5-inch angled sash + 2-2.5 inch angled), open and stir paint, pour into work pots, position ladder/scaffold per access tier. Per-session setup.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per session. Includes ladder/scaffold positioning per access tier.

tasks.name: Equipment Setup — Spray
tasks.description: Set up airless sprayer: flush lines, load paint, adjust pressure, select tip (211 for trim enamel), test pattern on scrap. Position spray rig and hose routing. Per-session setup.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per session. Spray setup takes longer than brush setup.

tasks.name: Landscape Ground Protection Setup
tasks.description: Lay drop cloths or poly sheeting over landscape areas below window work zones. Catches scraping debris, power wash runoff, and paint drips. Upgrades to full_cover for spray application. Upgrades to 6-mil poly for RRP containment. Shared protection zone with exterior trim RP.
tasks.notes: RP-specific. Shared zone with SF_TRIM_EXT_RP — first spec in elevation sequence owns setup. Cross-spec deduplication rule U-004.

tasks.name: Hardscape/Walkway Protection Setup
tasks.description: Lay drop cloth runners over walkways and patio surfaces below window work zones. Upgrades to full_cover for spray or RRP. Shared zone with exterior trim RP.
tasks.notes: RP-specific. Shared zone with SF_TRIM_EXT_RP — cross-spec deduplication rule U-004.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape/hardscape ground protection → Glass masking (mandatory) → Hardware removal → Weatherstrip protection → Sill protection → Casing protection → Siding masking (spray only) → Equipment setup. All setup complete before assessment begins.

sop_modules.name: Condition Assessment — Inspect, Adhesion Test, Chalk Test, Moisture Check, Glazing Assess, Rot Probe, Sash Operation
sop_modules.description: RP-specific assessment phase. Visual condition inspection (DSD rating, photograph defects), ASTM D3359 adhesion test at representative sections, chalk test (white cloth rub — exterior-specific), moisture check (sill/bottom rail/end grain — exterior windows are high moisture exposure), glazing compound assessment (older wood windows), rot probe (press/probe for soft wood — exterior-specific), sash operation test (pre-paint baseline). Results drive downstream task activation: primer selection, prep intensity, condition scale assignment. NO coating ID test needed (RC-003 — exterior paint is predominantly acrylic latex). 100% RP_NEW tasks. FIXED time per window.

tasks.name: Visual Condition Inspection — All Exterior Window Surfaces
tasks.description: Scan all exterior window surfaces (frame, sash, muntins, stool/apron) from ground and at working height. Map cracking, peeling, adhesion failure, chalking, fading, weathering damage, and paint film buildup. Assign condition_scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) based on worst-condition area per worst-state-wins rule. Photograph defects. Document scope of scraping, feathering, and treatment needed.

quality_notes.QT3: Standard visual with work light, document visible defects
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan with raking light, photograph all defect areas, per-surface assessment
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, multiple passes, full photographic documentation per surface

tasks.notes: Exterior windows exposed to UV, rain, thermal cycling — wider range of failure modes than interior. Height access may limit inspection at upper stories.

tasks.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
tasks.description: Perform cross-hatch tape test per ASTM D3359 at representative sections. Test at minimum 2 locations per window (frame + sash). Critical for exterior windows due to UV degradation and thermal cycling stress on coating adhesion. Results determine if full prime or spot prime is required.
tasks.notes: Pass result + SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT = skip full prime (ROUND_XWRP_2FINISH). Fail result = full prime required regardless of visual condition.

tasks.name: Chalk Test (White Cloth Rub)
tasks.description: Rub clean white cloth across painted exterior window surfaces to detect chalking. Exterior-specific test — chalking is a UV degradation failure mode that does not occur on interior surfaces. Grade: none (clean cloth), light (faint transfer), heavy (obvious powdery transfer). Heavy chalking triggers chalk-binding primer and chalk remediation prep.
tasks.notes: Exterior-only assessment. Chalking drives SS_EXT_CHALKING state and triggers SYS_PRIMER_EXT_CHALK_BINDING.

tasks.name: Moisture Check — Sill, Bottom Rail, End Grain
tasks.description: Moisture meter reading on exterior sill, sash bottom rail, and exposed end-grain areas. Exterior windows are high moisture exposure — rain, condensation, capillary wicking at end-grain. Flag active moisture sources for remediation. Moisture content >15% is STOP WORK for coating application on that surface until source is resolved and wood dries to <12%.
tasks.notes: Exterior windows have higher moisture risk than interior due to weather exposure. End-grain wicking is the primary moisture entry path on wood windows.

tasks.name: Glazing Compound Assessment (Older Wood Windows)
tasks.description: Inspect glazing compound condition on older single-pane and TDL wood windows. Probe test for firmness and adhesion. Classify: intact (paint over), cracked but adhered (spot repair + cure + paint), failed (scope-limited repair <25% of perimeter — beyond 25% is re-glaze scope). Modern IG units and vinyl/aluminum-clad windows have no exposed compound — skip.
tasks.notes: Exterior glazing deteriorates faster than interior due to UV and thermal cycling. Scope-limited to <25% perimeter repair (vs interior <20%).

tasks.name: Rot Probe — Press/Probe for Soft Wood
tasks.description: Probe exterior window wood at sill, bottom rail, and end-grain areas for surface-softened or punky wood. Use awl or screwdriver to press-test suspect areas. Exterior-specific — rot is weather-driven and does not occur on interior windows. Grade: sound (no probe penetration), surface-soft (wood hardener scope), punky/structural (carpentry referral — outside painting scope). Surface-soft triggers TSK_XWRP_WOOD_HARDEN in prep.
tasks.notes: Exterior-only assessment. Structural rot = HARD STOP for that window unit — refer to carpentry. Surface-soft = wood hardener in prep module.

tasks.name: Sash Operation Test (Pre-Paint)
tasks.description: Open and close all operable sashes before painting to identify binding, paint lock, or mechanical issues. Document sash operation status per sash. Pre-paint operation test establishes baseline — contractor is not responsible for pre-existing mechanical failures. Identifies sashes that may need sash break at 24/48 hrs post-cure.
tasks.notes: Skip for fixed windows (no operable sashes). Exterior window operation affected by paint buildup from multiple repaints and weather swelling.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition inspection first → Chalk test → Adhesion test → Moisture check → Rot probe (wood only) → Glazing compound assessment (older wood only) → Sash operation test. Assessment results determine which prep and prime tasks activate downstream.

sop_modules.name: Prep — Power Wash, Degloss/Scuff, Scrape/Feather, Chalk Remediation, Mildew Treatment, Caulk Repair, Glazing Repair, Wood Hardener, Substrate-Specific Prep
sop_modules.description: Condition-driven prep module for all exterior window surfaces. Power wash per elevation (replaces interior TSP hand-wash). Degloss/scuff sound existing paint. Scrape and feather failing/peeling areas. Chalk remediation for SS_EXT_CHALKING. Mildew/algae biocide treatment. Caulk assess/repair per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol. Glazing repair (scope-limited <25%). Wood hardener on surface-softened areas. Scuff exposed aluminum / clean exposed vinyl for cladding-specific prep. Condition modifiers: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.5x, POOR=2.0x on prep tasks. EA-based rates with size/type/muntin/height/condition/RRP modifiers.

tasks.name: Power Wash Exterior Windows (Per Elevation)
tasks.description: Low-pressure power wash (500-1000 PSI) all exterior window surfaces on the elevation. Removes dirt, cobwebs, mildew, chalk residue, loose paint, and surface contaminants. Careful at glazing joints and weatherstrip. Allow 24-48 hr dry before coating. Replaces interior TSP hand-wash. Per-elevation FIXED time task.
tasks.notes: Per-elevation task. Cross-spec deduplication rule U-003: if power wash already performed by another spec on same elevation, skip. Allow full dry time before any coating.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED — replaces interior TSP wash; per-elevation FIXED vs per-window EA

tasks.name: Degloss/Scuff Existing Paint
tasks.description: Chemical degloss (liquid sander wipe-on) or mechanical scuff (150-180 grit) on all previously painted exterior window surfaces. Creates adhesion profile for primer or finish coat. Chemical degloss preferred for sash profiles, muntin edges, and detail areas that sanding blocks cannot reach. For GOOD condition (SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT), degloss/scuff may be the only prep task needed.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss — chemical or mechanical on all accessible surfaces
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification on profiles
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification and spot adhesion re-test

tasks.notes: Skip for SS_EXT_PEELING (full scrape renders degloss redundant). Skip for SS_EXT_CHALKING (chalk remediation + chalk-binding primer path).
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED — RP degloss existing paint vs NC bare wood sanding

tasks.name: Scrape Failing Paint and Feather Edges
tasks.description: Scrape all failing, peeling, flaking, or loose paint from exterior window surfaces (frame, sash, muntins, stool/apron). Feather-sand all scrape edges to create smooth transition. Carbide scraper for exterior paint buildup. Muntin edges and sash profiles require careful contour scraping. Non-negotiable feathering at all tiers. Collect scraping debris for cleanup (RRP: into containment).

quality_notes.QT3: Remove all failing paint, feather edges — no visible ridge at 6 ft
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive scrape + near-invisible feathering at 3 ft
quality_notes.QT5: Critical scrape + perfect feathering — no ridge at arm's length

tasks.notes: Condition-driven intensity: FAIR = moderate scraping; POOR = heavy scraping (2.0x condition modifier). RRP doubles scraping time (wet methods required).

tasks.name: Chalk Remediation (Chalk-Binding Primer Prep)
tasks.description: Pre-treat chalking exterior surfaces before chalk-binding primer application. Power wash (already done) loosens heavy chalk; follow with chemical chalk remover on stubborn areas. Wipe and verify — white cloth test should show minimal residual chalk after treatment. Residual chalk will be bound by chalk-binding primer.
tasks.notes: Exterior-specific. Chalking is UV degradation — does not occur on interior surfaces. Chalk-binding primer (SYS_PRIMER_EXT_CHALK_BINDING) follows this task.

tasks.name: Mildew/Algae Biocide Treatment
tasks.description: Apply biocide solution to mildew or algae-affected exterior window areas. Common on north-facing elevations, shaded areas, and near ground level. Allow full contact/kill time per product directions. Rinse and allow dry before priming.
tasks.notes: Exterior-specific. Mildew/algae driven by moisture and shade exposure. Must treat before any coating — mildew will grow through new paint.

tasks.name: Assess and Repair Failed Caulk — Frame-to-Casing Joints
tasks.description: Inspect all existing caulk at frame-to-casing junction per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol. Remove and replace cracked, shrunk, or failed sections with acrylic latex caulk. Caulk at frame-to-casing junction is THIS spec's responsibility (not trim spec). Exterior caulk failure is more common than interior due to thermal cycling and UV. Estimated 20-40% of joints need replacement in typical exterior RP.

quality_notes.QT3: Replace visibly failed sections — cracked or separated joints
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect and failed joints
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, replace all joints not in perfect condition, perfect tooled bead

tasks.notes: Per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol: trace water path from top of window downward, caulk every joint where water could enter.

tasks.name: Spot Repair Failed Glazing Compound
tasks.description: Remove and replace failed glazing compound on older single-pane and TDL wood windows. Scope-limited to <25% of total glazing perimeter — beyond 25% is a re-glaze scope requiring separate trade estimate. Apply new glazing compound (acrylic or DAP), tool smooth, allow cure time per product specs before priming. Modern IG units have no exposed compound — skip.

quality_notes.QT3: Replace obviously failed sections. Smooth tool. Functional repair.
quality_notes.QT4: Replace all cracked or deteriorated sections. Clean tool lines.
quality_notes.QT5: Replace all imperfect sections. Crisp clean tool lines matching original profile.

tasks.notes: Exterior glazing deteriorates faster than interior due to UV and thermal cycling. Scope-limited to <25% perimeter.

tasks.name: Apply Wood Hardener to Surface-Softened Areas
tasks.description: Apply liquid wood hardener/consolidant to surface-softened wood areas identified during rot probe assessment. Penetrates and stabilizes softened wood fibers. Target areas: sill, bottom rail, end-grain. Apply by brush, allow full cure per product directions (typically 2-4 hrs) before sanding and priming. Structural rot is outside painting scope — this task addresses surface softening only.
tasks.notes: Exterior-specific. Triggered by rot probe assessment finding surface-soft wood. Structural rot = HARD STOP (carpentry referral).

tasks.name: Scuff-Sand Exposed Aluminum Cladding
tasks.description: Scuff-sand exposed aluminum cladding areas with 180-220 grit to create mechanical bonding profile for DTM spot primer. Required at areas where factory finish has failed, been scratched, or where aluminum is exposed. Do not sand intact painted areas — degloss/scuff handles those.
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC full-surface scuff. RP targets only exposed/damaged aluminum areas needing DTM spot prime.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_XWIN_SCUFF_SAND_ALUM — RP targets exposed areas only vs NC full surface

tasks.name: Clean Exposed Vinyl Cladding
tasks.description: Clean exposed vinyl cladding areas with TSP or vinyl-safe cleaner. No sanding on vinyl — creates micro-scratches that trap dirt. Clean only. Required at areas where factory finish has failed or vinyl is exposed and needs bonding primer.
tasks.notes: MODIFIED from NC full-surface clean. RP targets only exposed/damaged vinyl areas needing PVC bonding spot prime. NEVER sand vinyl.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_XWIN_CLEAN_VINYL — RP targets exposed areas only vs NC full surface

tasks.name: Clean Dust After Wood Sanding/Scraping
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust, degloss residue, scraping debris, and prep dust from exterior window wood surfaces with tack cloth or compressed air. Surface must be clean to touch before primer or finish application.
tasks.notes: Exterior dust cleanup may use compressed air in addition to tack cloth (outdoor context allows blowing). RRP: use HEPA vacuum instead of blowing.

tasks.name: Clean Dust After Aluminum Scuff-Sand
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from exposed aluminum areas with tack cloth. Surface must be clean and free of aluminum dust before DTM spot primer application.
tasks.notes: Aluminum dust interferes with DTM primer adhesion — thorough cleaning critical.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Power wash (per elevation, 24-48 hr dry) → Mildew/algae treatment (if present) → Chalk remediation (if SS_EXT_CHALKING) → Scrape/feather (if FAIR/POOR) → Degloss/scuff (if SOUND/FAILING) → Caulk assess/repair → Glazing repair (older wood) → Wood hardener (surface-soft areas) → Scuff aluminum / clean vinyl (cladding-specific) → Dust clean. All prep must be complete and dry before prime.

sop_modules.name: Prime — State-Driven Primer Application (Brush/Spray + Cladding-Specific Spot Prime)
sop_modules.description: State-driven primer module. Primer product determined by substrate state and cladding: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT with verified adhesion = skip prime (ROUND_XWRP_2FINISH). SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT/PEELING = acrylic stain-block primer (SYS_PRIMER_EXT_ACRYLIC_STAINBLOCK). SS_EXT_CHALKING = chalk-binding primer (SYS_PRIMER_EXT_CHALK_BINDING). Cladding-specific spot prime: aluminum exposed areas = corrosion-inhibiting DTM (SYS_PRIMER_ALUMINUM_DTM), vinyl exposed areas = PVC bonding (SYS_PRIMER_EXT_PVC_BONDING). Brush/spray variants match finish method. RP primes spot or full depending on condition (NC primes full surface of bare substrate).

tasks.name: Brush Primer on Exterior Window (State-Driven)
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to exterior window surfaces using 1.5-inch angled sash brush (sash, muntins, detail work) and 2-2.5 inch brush (frame faces, stool/apron). Primer product varies by substrate state: acrylic stain-block for FAILING/PEELING, chalk-binding for CHALKING. Work systematically at elevation. Full-surface or spot prime based on condition assessment.
tasks.notes: Skip for SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion verified (ROUND_XWRP_2FINISH). QT5 adds second prime coat (ROUND_XWRP_PRIME_2PRIME_2FINISH or ROUND_XWRP_2PRIME_2FINISH).
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_XWIN_PRIME_BRUSH_WOOD — RP state-driven vs NC cladding-driven

tasks.name: Spray Primer on Exterior Window (State-Driven)
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to exterior window surfaces via airless sprayer (310-411 tip). Requires additional siding/casing masking. Primer product varies by substrate state. Consistent mil thickness across all window surfaces.
tasks.notes: Skip for SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion verified. Spray primer requires full adjacent surface masking.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED from TSK_XWIN_PRIME_SPRAY_WOOD — RP state-driven vs NC cladding-driven

tasks.name: Spot Prime Exposed Aluminum with DTM Corrosion-Inhibiting Primer
tasks.description: Brush-apply corrosion-inhibiting DTM primer (SYS_PRIMER_ALUMINUM_DTM) to exposed aluminum cladding areas. Spot priming only — targets areas where factory finish has failed or been removed during prep. Must be applied over mechanical bonding profile from scuff-sand. Brush only — spot application too small for spray.
tasks.notes: Cladding-specific spot prime. Applied in addition to general state-driven prime (not instead of). Brush only regardless of finish method.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED — RP spot prime on exposed aluminum vs NC full-surface prime

tasks.name: Spot Prime Exposed Vinyl with PVC Bonding Primer
tasks.description: Brush-apply PVC bonding primer (SYS_PRIMER_EXT_PVC_BONDING) to exposed vinyl cladding areas. Spot priming only — targets areas where factory finish has failed or been removed. Standard primers will NOT bond to vinyl. Recoat within 1 week or primer loses flexibility. Brush only — spot application too small for spray.
tasks.notes: Cladding-specific spot prime. Standard primers will NOT bond to vinyl. Recoat window within 1 week of bonding primer application. Brush only regardless of finish method.
tasks.transfer_source: MODIFIED — RP spot prime on exposed vinyl vs NC full-surface prime

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Cladding-specific spot prime first (DTM aluminum or PVC bonding vinyl), then general state-driven prime coat (acrylic stain-block or chalk-binding). Spot prime addresses exposed substrate; general prime addresses overall condition. Allow full dry per product specs before interstage or finish.

sop_modules.name: Interstage — Intercoat Inspection, Sand, Repair, Dust Clean
sop_modules.description: Between-coat maintenance cycle for fine-finish exterior window surfaces. Inspect coat, sand between coats, repair defects, dust clean. Runs between each coat pair. DIRECT transfer from NC MOD_XWIN_INTERSTAGE — identical process once surface is prepped and primed. Sanding discipline varies by QT: QT3 none/spot, QT4 220-grit, QT5 hand-sand 220/320.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat. For prime+2finish: runs after prime, after finish 1. For 2finish (no prime): runs after finish 1 only.

tasks.name: Intercoat Inspection
tasks.description: Visual inspection of applied coat on all exterior window surfaces (frame, sash, muntins, stool/apron). Look for dust nibs, brush marks, missed areas, runs, sags, insects, and surface texture issues. Exterior inspections include weather-related defects (blistering from sun exposure, insect embedment).

quality_notes.QT3: Quick glance at 6 feet — obvious defects only
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects per surface
quality_notes.QT5: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance including muntin edges

tasks.name: Sand Between Coats
tasks.description: Between-coat sanding on exterior window surfaces. QT3: none or spot sand nibs only. QT4: light full sand 220-grit. QT5: thorough hand-sand 220/320. Sash profiles and muntin edges require contour sanding sponge. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot sand only — visible nibs and rough spots. 220 grit.
quality_notes.QT4: Light full sand — entire surface including sash and muntin profiles. 220 grit.
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough full sand — every surface and edge. 220/320 grit. Uniform scratch pattern.

tasks.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth or compressed air before next coat application. Critical for dust-free finish on window surfaces. Exterior allows compressed air blowing (RRP: HEPA vacuum only).

tasks.name: Spot Repair Intercoat Defects
tasks.description: Address defects found during intercoat inspection. Fill dust nibs, sand out brush marks, touch up missed areas. Spot coat repaired areas to build film thickness before next full coat.

quality_notes.QT3: Repair obvious defects only — runs, sags, holidays
quality_notes.QT4: Repair all marked defects visible at 3 feet
quality_notes.QT5: Repair all defects regardless of size

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Sand → Dust clean → Spot repair. Runs after each coat except the final coat.

sop_modules.name: Finish — Coat Application (Brush/Spray) + Muntin Detail + Sash Sequence
sop_modules.description: Finish coat application and sash blocking prevention. 2 finish coats standard (QT3-QT5). Fine-finish coating systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). 1/16-inch glass lap for weather seal. Sash sequence for double-hung blocking prevention (reversal, dry posture, periodic movement, channel lubrication) — DIRECT transfer from NC. Apply, tip once, walk away. BLOCKING PREVENTION: paint sashes in operating position, move periodically during dry.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat 1
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat with 1.5-inch angled sash brush (sash, muntins) and 2-2.5 inch brush (frame faces, stool/apron). Work systematically: horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles (with the grain). 1/16-inch glass lap at frame-to-glass edge for weather seal. Apply, tip once, walk away — short working time products demand proper first-pass technique.
tasks.notes: 1/16-inch glass lap is MANDATORY weather seal on exterior windows. Horizontal rails first, then vertical stiles.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat 1
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat via airless sprayer (211 tip for trim enamel). Systematic pass: frame, sash, muntins, stool/apron. Consistent distance and speed for uniform mil thickness. Back-brush on detailed profiles as needed.
tasks.notes: Spray savings limited (~25-30% faster) due to mandatory back-brushing on detailed profiles.

tasks.name: Muntin Bar Detail — Coat 1
tasks.description: Detail painting of TDL/SDL muntin bars with 1.5-inch angular sash brush. Each bar face and edges, glass lap at each bar-to-glass junction. Precision work — TDL muntins are the highest skill-demand component. First coat.
tasks.notes: SDL: applied bar painting (moderate time). TDL: individual bar faces + edges + glass lap per junction (high time — 1.75x muntin modifier).

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat 2
tasks.description: Apply second finish coat. Faster pace than coat 1 — consistent substrate. Same technique and philosophy. Final coat quality is paramount — this is the visible finish.
tasks.notes: Final coat. No interstage after this coat — goes directly to sash sequence (if double-hung) then cleanup.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat 2
tasks.description: Apply second finish coat via airless sprayer. Faster pace than coat 1 — consistent substrate. Final coat quality is paramount.
tasks.notes: Final coat. No interstage after this coat.

tasks.name: Muntin Bar Detail — Coat 2
tasks.description: Detail painting of TDL/SDL muntin bars — second coat. Same technique as coat 1. Final coat on muntins — highest scrutiny.
tasks.notes: Final muntin coat. QT4/QT5: inspect each muntin bar after coat 2 for holidays.

tasks.name: Sash Reversal (Double-Hung)
tasks.description: Reverse sash positions on double-hung windows after painting exposed surfaces. Slide upper sash down, lower sash up to expose unpainted sash channels and meeting rail areas. Ensures complete coverage of all surfaces including those hidden in normal operating position.
tasks.notes: Double-hung only. Sash must be reversed during painting to access meeting rail and channel surfaces.

tasks.name: Position Sash for Drying (Double-Hung)
tasks.description: After painting both sash positions, set sashes in partially open 'dry posture' — upper sash cracked down 1 inch, lower sash cracked up 1 inch. Prevents sash-to-frame paint bonding during cure. Critical for blocking prevention.
tasks.notes: Double-hung only. NEVER fully close sashes during drying. Dry posture prevents adhesion bond between sash and stops.

tasks.name: Periodic Sash Movement During Dry (Double-Hung)
tasks.description: Move sashes periodically during cure to prevent adhesion bond formation. Slide each sash 2-3 inches in each direction at 30-60 minute intervals during initial cure. Critical for double-hung windows where friction surfaces generate maximum blocking force. RP has higher blocking risk due to existing paint buildup.
tasks.notes: Double-hung only. 30-60 minute intervals during initial cure (first 2-4 hours). RP: increased blocking risk from paint buildup layers.

tasks.name: Lubricate Sash Channels (Double-Hung)
tasks.description: Apply dry lubricant (wax or silicone-free dry spray) to sash channels after final coat has dried to tack-free stage. Reduces friction and prevents future binding. Do NOT use WD-40 or silicone-based lubricants — they interfere with future paint adhesion.
tasks.notes: Double-hung only. Dry lubricant only — no silicone-based products. Applied after tack-free, before full cure.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Finish coat 1 (brush/spray) → Muntin detail coat 1 (TDL/SDL) → Interstage module → Finish coat 2 (brush/spray) → Muntin detail coat 2 (TDL/SDL) → Sash sequence (double-hung only: reverse → dry posture → periodic move → lubricate channels).

sop_modules.name: Cleanup — Final Inspect, Touch-Up, Glass Cleanup, Protection Teardown, Hardware Reinstall, Customer Walkthrough, Cure Advisory, Sash Break
sop_modules.description: Full cleanup module for exterior window repaint. Final inspection and touch-up. Glass scraping after cure (razor scrape excess paint beyond 1/16-inch glass lap). Protection teardown (glass masking, sill, casing, siding, landscape, hardscape). Hardware reinstall and weatherstrip reinstall. Customer walkthrough (RP-specific). Cure advisory (7-14 days before fully closing sashes). Sash break at 24/48 hrs to prevent adhesion bond (RP-specific — existing paint buildup increases blocking risk). Equipment cleanup. RP adds customer walkthrough, cure advisory, and sash break vs NC.

tasks.name: Final Window Inspection
tasks.description: Final quality check of all painted exterior window surfaces. Verify coverage uniformity, sheen consistency, no runs/sags/holidays, clean glass lap line, hardware operation, sash positioning. QT-scaled inspection rigor.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects, uniform sheen
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — no visible defects on frame, sash, and muntins
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length under natural light — zero tolerance across all surfaces

tasks.name: Touch-Up Defects
tasks.description: Address any remaining defects found during final inspection. Touch up with same finish product. Spot sand and recoat as needed. QT-scaled effort.

quality_notes.QT4: Address all visible defects — blend touch-up into surrounding finish
quality_notes.QT5: Address every imperfection — full coat over spot repairs if needed to equalize sheen

tasks.name: Glass Scraping / Cleanup
tasks.description: After cure: score paint edge on glass with sharp razor blade. Scrape excess paint from glass. For 1/16-inch weather seal lap, score precisely at 1/16 inch from frame edge. Multi-pane TDL windows take significantly longer. Replace razor blades frequently for clean cuts.
tasks.notes: Must wait for cure before scraping. TDL windows: each muntin bar junction adds scoring work. Replace razor blades frequently — dull blades scratch glass.

tasks.name: Remove Glass Masking — Tape and Film
tasks.description: Remove static-cling film and tape from glass panes. Pull tape at 45-degree angle. Remove while finish is slightly tacky for clean edge, or after full cure with scoring.

tasks.name: Remove Glass Masking — Liquid Mask Peel
tasks.description: Peel dried liquid masking product from TDL glass panes. Score edge with razor at frame-to-glass junction, then peel film from glass surface. Inspect for residue.

tasks.name: Remove Glass Masking — TDL Individual Pane Tape
tasks.description: Remove individual pane tape and film from TDL Low-E glass panes. Highest masking removal labor — each small pane has its own tape and film.

tasks.name: Reinstall Window Hardware
tasks.description: Reinstall removed window hardware (locks, lifts, sash pulls, crank handles). Verify operation. Check for paint transfer to hardware — clean if needed.
tasks.notes: Skip for fixed windows (no hardware removed). Verify hardware operates smoothly after reinstall.

tasks.name: Reinstall Weatherstripping
tasks.description: Reinstall removed friction-fit weatherstripping or remove deep-tape protection from non-removable weatherstripping. Verify seal integrity. Replace damaged weatherstripping if needed (notify homeowner of replacement cost).
tasks.notes: Skip for fixed windows. Verify seal after reinstall.

tasks.name: Remove Sill Protection
tasks.description: Remove tape and paper/film from exterior sill. Check for adhesive residue — remove with mineral spirits if needed.

tasks.name: Remove Casing Protection
tasks.description: Remove tape at casing-to-frame junction. Pull at 45-degree angle for clean edge.

tasks.name: Remove Siding Masking (Spray Only)
tasks.description: Remove paper and tape siding masking from around window perimeter. Spray method only.

tasks.name: Equipment Cleanup
tasks.description: Clean brushes, spray equipment (if used). Proper storage or disposal of consumables. All waterborne products — water cleanup. Fixed time per session regardless of window count.
tasks.notes: FIXED time per session. Includes scraping debris collection and disposal.

tasks.name: Customer Walkthrough
tasks.description: Walk exterior window areas with homeowner. Inspect finish quality from ground level, verify sash operation, confirm glass cleanliness, confirm satisfaction. Address any touch-up requests on the spot. Explain cure advisory and sash break schedule. RP-specific — repaint work requires client sign-off.
tasks.notes: RP-specific. Per-project FIXED time. Lead painter conducts walkthrough.

tasks.name: Cure Advisory Communication
tasks.description: Advise homeowner on cure time expectations: 7-14 days before fully closing/latching sashes. Provide written cure advisory. Explain that enamels reach full hardness slowly — premature full closure risks adhesion bonding between sash and frame. Exterior windows cure slower in cool/humid conditions.
tasks.notes: RP-specific. Combined with customer walkthrough visit. Written advisory recommended for liability protection.

tasks.name: Break Sash Free (24/48 Hr Post-Cure Return)
tasks.description: Return at 24-48 hours post-cure to break all operable sashes free. Score paint bridge with putty knife before opening. Open and close each sash to prevent adhesion bond between sash and frame/stops. RP has higher blocking risk due to existing paint buildup from multiple repaints. Do NOT force — if sash is stuck, score carefully and apply gentle pressure.
tasks.notes: RP-specific. Requires return visit at 24-48 hrs. May be combined with glass cleanup visit. Skip for fixed windows (no operable sashes). Exterior RP has highest blocking risk due to paint layer buildup.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspect → Touch-up → Glass scraping (after cure) → Masking removal → Hardware reinstall → Weatherstrip reinstall → Sill/casing/siding protection teardown → Customer walkthrough + Cure advisory → Equipment clean. Sash break occurs on separate return visit at 24-48 hrs post-cure.

sop_modules.name: Lead-Safe RRP Exterior Containment (Shared Module)
sop_modules.description: Shared exterior lead-safe RRP module. Conditional on PS_EXT_META.FLAG.PRE_1978 = true and positive lead test. Per-elevation setup: 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745. Windows are HIGH RISK for lead paint — friction surfaces on operable sashes are the #1 residential lead dust generator. Shared across all exterior RP specs. This module is NOT owned by this spec — it is a shared module referenced by all exterior RP specs.

tasks.name: Lead Screening Test (XRF or Swab)
tasks.description: Perform lead test at representative areas per elevation. XRF preferred; lead swab test acceptable. Test at minimum 2 locations per elevation (frame + sash). Windows are high-risk for lead paint — friction surfaces generate lead dust during sash operation.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. Results gate all subsequent RRP tasks and 2.0x prep modifier.

tasks.name: RRP Exterior Containment Setup (Per Elevation)
tasks.description: Install 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP Rule. Secure edges with weights or stakes. Install warning signage. Restrict area to certified RRP personnel only. Per-elevation setup.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. 6-mil poly minimum per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.

tasks.name: RRP Wet Scraping Method
tasks.description: Wet-scrape method for lead paint removal. Mist surface with water before scraping to minimize dust generation. All scraping debris falls into containment below. EPA RRP requirement when disturbing lead paint.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Applied per window (EA). RRP doubles prep time on scraping tasks (2.0x modifier captured in FAC_XWRP_RRP).

tasks.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
tasks.description: HEPA vacuum all surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance to capture lead-contaminated dust. Required by EPA RRP Rule. Windows generate high dust volume from sash channel and frame scraping.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Applied per window (EA). Required after EVERY sanding/scraping disturbance — not just once.

tasks.name: RRP Exterior Containment Teardown (Per Elevation)
tasks.description: Remove containment poly, fold inward to capture debris, bag for lead-safe disposal. Verify cleaning standard per EPA (visual + wet wipe test on hard surfaces, HEPA vacuum on soil). Per-elevation teardown.
tasks.notes: Shared task. Per-elevation FIXED time. Must pass EPA cleaning verification standard before removing containment.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Lead screen first → Containment setup (per elevation) → All paint disturbance tasks use wet methods within containment → HEPA vacuum after each disturbance → Containment teardown (per elevation, after all work complete on that elevation).

task_count_summary.reconciliation_note: Research projected ~63 tasks based on 38 DIRECT + 8 MODIFIED + 22 RP_NEW - 2 double-counted (POWER_WASH, DEGLOSS_SCUFF in both MODIFIED and RP_NEW) - 5 NOT_APPLICABLE = 61 XWRP-prefixed tasks. This spec actualizes 64 XWRP-prefixed tasks + 5 shared TSK_RRP_EXT_* tasks = 69 total. Difference: 2 RP_NEW entries (RRP_CONTAINMENT_SETUP and RRP_CONTAINMENT_TEARDOWN) were absorbed into the shared MOD_RRP_EXT_CONTAINMENT module (5 tasks), yielding net +3 vs projection.

module_sequence.notes: RRP containment setup (if applicable) occurs after general setup but before assessment. Assessment drives prep/prime task activation. Interstage runs between each coat pair (per run_rule). Finish includes sash sequence tasks for double-hung. Cleanup includes return visit tasks (sash break at 24/48 hrs).
